questions.question: Explain convection in a pot of water heated from below, using the words expand and density, and describe how to show the convection current.
questions.expected_answer: Water at the bottom is heated, its particles move faster and spread apart, so it expands and becomes less dense; it rises, and cooler, denser water sinks to take its place, is heated and rises in turn, forming a circulating convection current that carries heat through the water. Show it by placing a few potassium permanganate crystals at the bottom on one side of a beaker of water and heating gently below them: the purple colour rises, spreads across the top, sinks on the other side and returns along the bottom.

questions.question: Describe the convection current in a room warmed by a heater and explain why heaters should be placed low and air conditioners high.
questions.expected_answer: Air near the heater is warmed, expands, becomes less dense and rises to the ceiling, spreads across, cools, becomes denser and sinks on the far side, then flows back along the floor to the heater. Heaters placed low warm the air that then rises and circulates through the whole room; air conditioners placed high produce cool, dense air that sinks and pushes warm air up to be cooled, setting up a cooling current.

questions.question: Explain how a sea breeze forms on a sunny day and how a land breeze forms at night.
questions.expected_answer: By day, land heats up faster than the sea, so the air above the land is warmed, expands, becomes less dense and rises; cooler, denser air from over the sea flows in to replace it, giving a sea breeze from sea to land. At night the land cools faster than the sea, so the air over the sea is warmer and rises, and cooler air flows from the land towards the sea, a land breeze.
